answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a copper bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. Verified history accrues like layers of onyx - hard, slow to build, and easy to audit - while newcomers start with a tiny ember of trust that only grows through honest, attested work. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand bonds and earns no reputation, so sybil operators pay more than they can gain.
